root_idea.summary: A semantic orientation toward moving something aside or removing it so that what it covered is exposed.
root_idea.development: The attested uses extend from physically stripping a hide or covering, to removing something from its place, clearing or dispersing what has been removed, and figuratively describing fear as having gone away.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation headword كَشَطَ rather than the Quranic passive inflection كُشِطَتْ.

senses.definition: To strip away or remove a covering or outer layer from what it covers; in the Quranic use, the heaven is stripped away or removed from its place.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence is passive and applies the image of removing a roof-like covering to the heaven. It is also interpreted as the heaven being pulled off and folded together.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remove a letter from its place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A cited conventional construction concerning the alteration or removal of a written letter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To skin a camel by removing its hide.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized camel-skinning usage; the evidence explicitly distinguishes it from the ordinary verb سَلَخَ in this context.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For one's fright or fear to be removed or go away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative passive or intransitive construction describing the departure of fear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For clouds to become disunited and disperse in the sky.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V intransitive usage, with clouds as the subject.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become removed or cleared away, as dust carried off by the wind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form VII intransitive usage describing material being cleared or blown away.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The stripped skin or hide of a slaughtered camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for the removed hide.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A slaughterer or skinner of camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An occupational noun associated with slaughtering or removing the hide from camels.
Plural designations reported for people associated with a skinned camel, distinct from the occupational sense of كَاشِطٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A slaughtered camel whose skin has been removed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participial description of the camel in that state.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Its covering-removal, letter-removal, camel-skinning, and figurative fear constructions are represented.
